Genomics pipeline in a VAST enclave tenant

the lab cluster · tenant rad-lab-enclave · 1000 Genomes 30x (open consent) · compute on client-n5
cluster DataEngine Trino function Open VMS ↗
Lab demonstration on public, open-consent data. It shows controls that inform a risk analysis; it is not a HIPAA compliance claim. The Data Engine trigger, CloudEvents and broker are real VAST Data Engine. The function runs on client-n5 in the DE handler shape, because no Kubernetes compute cluster is linked to this tenant. Timings come from a shared lab cluster (3 CNodes + 1 DBox) and are not a performance claim.

1 · The enclave boundary

One tenant with its own VIP pool and identity provider. One view, presented over NFS, S3 and the database API, governed by an S3-native view policy.

Enclave map: export and mount isolation (server-side host allow-list), a separate access-control domain (the tenant's own provider), and root squash.

2 · Who can do what · try it live

Each identity has one job, and every cell below is a real request sent now from n5. A deny counts only when the allow-path in the same column returns 200.

Enclave map: least privilege per role. Ingest can land files but cannot read them back. The analyst reads but cannot change anything. The auditor sees the audit trail and nothing in the cohort.

3 · Ingest → Data Engine trigger

An instrument or ingest service PUTs over S3 into incoming/. The element trigger rle-cohort-landing emits a CloudEvent per object. The index file lands last and acts as the completion marker.

–CloudEvents on rle-landing-events

4 · Transform → VAST DB

The function reads each landed file over NFS from the same view, as uid 7101 (rle-svc). VCF goes to variants and genotypes (sorted on chrom, pos), CRAM to cram_qc via samtools, POD5 to nanopore_runs, and the population file to samples.

5 · Ask the cohort

Live: rare (AF<1%) PASS carriers in a gene's promoter or upstream window, by superpopulation. Trino over VAST DB, as the analyst.

The same questions, measured three ways (latest run)

Each question runs three ways on the same view: VAST DB through Trino 478; the same tables written as Parquet files, read by Trino's Hive connector over S3; and bcftools 1.21 over NFS on the original files. Everything runs as the analyst, and the three answers are checked for identity.

6 · Audit: who read sample X's CRAM?

Protocol auditing writes into a VAST DB table. Pick a sample: the analyst reads its CRAM over NFS (O_DIRECT, because a client-cache hit sends no READ to VAST and so leaves nothing to audit) and over S3, and then the auditor queries the trail.

Latest 40 audit rows for the tenant
Enclave map: tenant-level audit that names the user, protocol, operation, status and bytes. Denied attempts are recorded too. The auditor role cannot read the cohort, and the analyst cannot read the audit trail.

7 · Controls, measured

Latest controls run: S3 identity policies, Tabular (VAST DB) access, NFS root squash, an identity policy enforced on an NFS uid, and the host allow-list.

8 · Reproducibility snapshot

One locked snapshot of the view freezes the VCF and CRAM objects and the VAST DB tables together, and stays readable through the SDK. Locked means delete is refused until it's unlocked. Indestructibility is armed cluster-wide, but it isn't used on this shared cluster.

9 · VAST Catalog: the query for research computing

File count and bytes by extension per owner uid. Rows are scoped to the caller's tenant: the same SQL run as the enclave analyst sees only the enclave.
